lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are playing Yes or No!
I will ask a question about an animal friend.
If you think yes, give a thumbs up. If you think no, shake your head.
Let's practice. Yes or no. Am I a bluebird?
Yes! I am Milo the bluebird! Good job.
Are you ready? Let's play!
Here is the polar bear. Look at that white, fluffy fur.
Yes or no. Is a polar bear's skin white?
No! Here is the fun fact. Under the fur, a polar bear's skin is black!
Look closer. Black skin, hiding under all that fur.
And the fur is not really white. Each hair is clear, like glass!
Under the skin, there is a thick layer of fat. It keeps the polar bear warm in the icy cold.
Next question. Yes or no. Can a polar bear swim?
Yes! Polar bears are super swimmers!
Look at those big front paws. They work like paddles in the water.
Each paw is as big as a dinner plate!
A polar bear can swim a very, very long way, without stopping to rest!
Its back legs steer, like the rudder of a boat.
Brrr! The water is icy cold. But the polar bear stays warm.
Say it with me. Polar bear skin is black!
Can you paddle your paws like a polar bear? Paddle, paddle, paddle!
Quick check! What color is a polar bear's skin? White? Or black?
Black! Black skin, under clear fur. Brilliant!
Clap your paws!
Here is the horse. Clip, clop!
Yes or no. Can a horse sleep standing up?
Yes! Here is the fun fact. A horse can sleep standing up!
But how can it sleep without falling over?
Its legs lock in place, so it does not fall over.
You have two legs. A horse has four! One, two, three, four.
For a big, deep sleep, the horse lies down on the soft ground.
A horse does not sleep all night like you. It takes lots of tiny naps!
Now look, a baby horse! A baby horse is called a foal.
A foal can stand up on its wobbly legs when it is only one hour old!
The mama horse feeds her foal with her milk.
Now you. Do you sleep standing up? Yes, or no?
No! You sleep lying down, in your cozy bed. But a horse can do both!
Say it with me. Horses can sleep standing up!
Can you stand very still and close your eyes? Shh. One, two, three.
Quick check! For a big, deep sleep, does a horse stand up? Or lie down?
It lies down! Good remembering!
Now wiggle and wake up. Good morning!
Here is the giraffe. Look at that long, long neck!
Yes or no. Does a giraffe have the same number of neck bones as you?
Yes! Here is the fun fact. A giraffe has seven neck bones. And so do you!
The giraffe's neck bones are just much, much bigger. Each one is almost as long as a ruler!
Let's count them. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven!
Next question. Yes or no. Does a tiny mouse have seven neck bones too?
Yes! A mouse has seven. You have seven. And the giraffe has seven!
Almost every furry animal has seven neck bones. Big or small!
Let's count on your fingers. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven!
And the giraffe's tongue is long too. Even longer than a ruler!
It uses that long tongue to grab leaves from the tall, tall trees.
Say it with me. Seven neck bones, just like me!
Can you touch your neck? Gently now. Nod your head. Yes, yes, yes!
Quick check! How many neck bones does a giraffe have? Five? Or seven?
Seven! Just like you!
Hold up seven fingers. Hooray!
Wow! What a great game. Let's play one more time, super fast!
Get ready!
Is a polar bear's skin white?
No! It is black!
Can a horse sleep standing up?
Yes! It can!
Does a giraffe have seven neck bones, like you?
Yes! Seven, just like you!
You learned so many new things today.
Paddle like a polar bear. Stand still like a horse. And nod like a giraffe!
Which answer surprised you the most?
One last question. Yes or no. Did you have fun today?
Yes! Me too!
Thank you for playing with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
